edges.description: Dysregulated phosphate handling favors calcium-phosphate precipitation along deep-brain microvascular structures.

Failed mitochondrial energy metabolism with raised intracellular inorganic phosphate in high-demand neurons and vascular endothelial cells favours calcium-phosphate precipitation at the same deep-brain microvascular sites the transporter and neurovascular-unit lesions act on.
Calcium-phosphate deposition along neurovascular structures manifests radiographically as bilateral intracranial calcifications.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function of CMPK2 causes mitochondria deficiency and brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: Here, we analyzed two brain calcification families and identified calcification co-segregated biallelic variants in the CMPK2 gene that disrupt mitochondrial functions.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function of CMPK2 causes mitochondria deficiency and brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: Notably, calcification developed in a progressive manner in the homozygous Cmpk2-KO mice thalamus region as well as in the Cmpk2-knock-in mice bearing the patient mutation, thus phenocopying the calcification pathology observed in the patients.

evidence.reference_title: The Genetics of Primary Familial Brain Calcification: A Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: Hitherto, seven genes have been associated with PFBC, including four dominant inherited genes (SLC20A2, PDGFRB, PDGFB, and XPR1) and three recessive inherited genes (MYORG, JAM2, and CMPK2).

nodes.description: SLC20A2 and XPR1 directly regulate inorganic phosphate influx and efflux, while NAA60 loss secondarily reduces SLC20A2 surface abundance and phosphate uptake. Together these defects dysregulate phosphate handling in the brain microvascular environment and promote calcium-phosphate deposition.

evidence.reference_title: Haploinsufficiency of the Primary Familial Brain Calcification Gene SLC20A2 Mediated by Disruption of a Regulatory Element.
evidence.snippet: Haploinsufficiency of SLC20A2, which encodes an inorganic phosphate importer, is a major cause of autosomal-dominant PFBC.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in XPR1 cause primary familial brain calcification associated with altered phosphate export.
evidence.snippet: These mutations alter phosphate export, implicating XPR1 and phosphate homeostasis in PFBC.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic NAA60 variants with impaired n-terminal acetylation capacity cause autosomal recessive primary familial brain calcifications.
evidence.snippet: In cells, loss of NAA60 caused reduced surface levels of SLC20A2 and a reduction in extracellular phosphate uptake.

nodes.description: Symptomatic dopaminergic therapy can improve PFBC-associated parkinsonism, although treatment may require adjustment because motor fluctuations and dyskinesia can emerge.

evidence.reference_title: Primary familial brain calcification presenting with parkinsonism and motor complications caused by a novel SLC20A2 variant: a case report.
evidence.snippet: This example expands the phenotype of SLC20A2-associated PFBC patients and shows the clinical efficacy of dopaminergic replacement treatment.

nodes.description: Bilateral intracranial calcification involving the basal ganglia and other deep brain regions is the defining radiographic hallmark of the disorder.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in JAM2 cause primary familial brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: Primary familial brain calcification is a monogenic disease characterized by bilateral calcifications in the basal ganglia and other brain regions, and commonly presents motor, psychiatric, and cognitive symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in JAM2 cause primary familial brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: Our study identifies a novel causative gene for primary familial brain calcification, whose vital function and high expression in the neurovascular unit further supports impairment of the neurovascular unit as the root of primary familial brain calcification pathogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: MYORG is associated with recessive primary familial brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: MYORG mutations are linked to a recessive form of primary familial brain calcification.

evidence.reference_title: MYORG is associated with recessive primary familial brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: the MYORG protein may interact with calcium channels expressed in astrocytes

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic NAA60 variants with impaired n-terminal acetylation capacity cause autosomal recessive primary familial brain calcifications.
evidence.snippet: This study establishes NAA60 as a causal gene for PFBC, provides a possible biochemical explanation of its disease-causing mechanisms and underscores NAA60-mediated Nt-acetylation of transmembrane proteins as a fundamental process for healthy neurobiological functioning.

nodes.description: CMPK2 loss of function depletes mitochondrial DNA and mitochondrial protein in neurons and vascular endothelial cells, two brain cell types with high energy expenditure, lowering ATP production, distorting cristae architecture, and raising intracellular inorganic phosphate. This is a third initiating axis in this disease, alongside the phosphate transporters and the neurovascular-unit genes, and it converges on the same deposition step.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function of CMPK2 causes mitochondria deficiency and brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: In situ hybridization and single-cell RNA sequencing revealed robust Cmpk2 expression in neurons and vascular endothelial cells (vECs), two cell types with high energy expenditure in the brain.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function of CMPK2 causes mitochondria deficiency and brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: The neurons in Cmpk2-knockout (KO) mice have fewer mitochondrial DNA copies, down-regulated mitochondrial proteins, reduced ATP production, and elevated intracellular inorganic phosphate (Pi) level, recapitulating the mitochondrial dysfunction observed in the PBMCs isolated from the FBC patients.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function of CMPK2 causes mitochondria deficiency and brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: Morphologically, the cristae architecture of the Cmpk2-KO murine neurons was also impaired.

evidence.reference_title: The Genetics of Primary Familial Brain Calcification: A Literature Review.
evidence.snippet: The function of currently known genes suggests that PFBC could be caused by the dysfunction of the neurovascular unit, the dysregulation of phosphate homeostasis, or mitochondrial dysfunction.

nodes.description: PFBC-linked PDGFB/PDGFRB and JAM2 defects impair pericyte-endothelial-astrocyte homeostasis, while related recessive pathways such as MYORG likely converge on the same neurovascular system. Reduced blood-brain barrier maintenance and cell-cell adhesion favor vascular and perivascular brain calcification.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding PDGF-B cause brain calcifications in humans and mice.
evidence.snippet: The occurrence of these calcium depositions depends on the loss of endothelial PDGF-B and correlates with the degree of pericyte and blood-brain barrier deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in JAM2 cause primary familial brain calcification.
evidence.snippet: We speculated that mutant JAM2 protein resulted in impaired cell-cell adhesion functions and reduced integrity of the neurovascular unit.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding PDGF-B cause brain calcifications in humans and mice.
evidence.snippet: Here we identify six families of different ancestry with nonsense and missense mutations in the gene encoding PDGF-B, the main ligand for PDGF-Rβ.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of the PDGFRB gene as a cause of idiopathic basal ganglia calcification.
evidence.snippet: Mutations of PDGFRB further support the involvement of this biological pathway in IBGC pathophysiology.

nodes.description: Parkinsonism is one of the most common symptomatic motor manifestations in clinically affected BSPDC/PFBC carriers.

evidence.reference_title: Primary brain calcification: an international study reporting novel variants and associated phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: A total of 81.5% of carriers were symptomatic and the most recurrent symptoms were parkinsonism, cognitive impairment, and psychiatric disturbances (52.3%, 40.9%, and 38.6% of symptomatic individuals, respectively), with a wide range of age at onset (from childhood to 81 years).
